clue.text: Rival ducks maintain very quiet whistle

indicators.note: the ducks hold or keep the quiet letters between them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the letter O; two ducks give OO
PP, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet
to whistle on someone is to inform, which in slang is to sing

explanation.surface: A rival tries to win by keeping the ducks utterly silent while whistling over them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maintain' puts PP inside the two O's; 'whistle' is the informer's slang, not a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing teams or candidates are rivals, set against each other in competition.

clue.text: Group of stars tackling saint's prayer

indicators.note: the constellation takes on, or grips, the saint, so the saint's letter goes inside it

parts.note: Orion is a well-known constellation, the Hunter
S is the standard abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A constellation is pictured wrestling with a saint's prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an old literary word for a spoken prayer.

clue.text: Cheeky lads hoard trendy images of celebs

indicators.note: the lads keep a store inside themselves, so the trendy word sits within them

parts.note: a young pup is a cheeky, impertinent youth
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Cheeky boys stash fashionable pictures of famous people.
explanation.definitionFit: Pin-ups are pictures of attractive celebrities pinned on walls by fans.

clue.text: French barman's burlesque denied run

indicators.note: the burlesque is refused one of its letters, so the run is taken away

parts.note: a burlesque is a mocking imitation, a satire
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A French bartender's comic show is barred from running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barman' is not a bartender: it is a man of bars, a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, and composers write music in bars.

clue.text: Archenemy is after northbound sailors, abducting one

indicators.note: the word is comes after the sailors piece
carrying off one, which is then taken away from the sailors
in a down clue, going north means the word is written upwards, so read the sailors backwards

parts.note: seamen are sailors
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: An archenemy follows sailors heading north and kidnaps one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northbound' reverses the sailors to give NEMAES, since a down entry is read upwards; 'abducting one' then takes out its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is a person's arch-rival or inescapable foe, named after the Greek goddess of retribution.

clue.text: Wine on board is appalling

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts the wine inside the ship's letters

parts.note: ships are written SS, steamship; going on board means inside them
hock is German white wine

explanation.surface: Drinking wine aboard ship is said to be appalling.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK goes inside SS: 'on board' is the convention for putting something within SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocks is a verb here: something appalling outrages, horrifies or scandalises people.

clue.text: Catch walrus for one suffering

parts.note: to catch a remark is to hear it
a walrus is one type of moustache, informally a tache

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to capture a walrus as a single example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walrus' is not the animal but the drooping moustache style.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional anguish or grief, a kind of suffering.

clue.text: Start of church ceremony broadcast raised standards

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word church is used

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word writes it upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A church service is broadcast at the start and lifts standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the standards by which something is judged.

clue.text: Go over in launch in a dream perhaps

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed inside the launch word

parts.note: to sling is to hurl or launch

indicators.note: in a down clue, over signals the word turned round

parts.note: to go is a coy euphemism for urinating, to pee

explanation.surface: Something goes over during a launch, as if in a dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is asleep may well be dreaming, so dreaming is one example of the state.

clue.text: Popular record setter's breaking any minute now

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: the setter's letters break into the record, splitting it

parts.note: a note is a written record
the setter refers to themselves; setter's is read as setter is, I'M

explanation.surface: A setter predicts that a popular record is about to be broken any minute.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means very soon or almost immediately, the same idea as any minute now.

clue.text: Local inexperienced model's introduced

indicators.note: the model is brought into the middle of the inexperienced word

parts.note: naive means inexperienced, unworldly
the Model T was Ford's famous car; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A green young model is introduced to the local scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a place is a local, someone born there.

clue.text: They may be small devices on shields

definitions.meaning: small weapons such as pistols and rifles are a class of firearms
heraldic designs painted on shields form a coat of armorial bearings

explanation.surface: Little emblems appear on shields.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons collectively and heraldic bearings are both called by this single word.

clue.text: Taskmaster has workmen collecting papers

indicators.note: the workmen gather the papers between them, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: work gives OP, short for opus, and men gives OR, other ranks in the army
the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: A taskmaster's labourers are out gathering the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workmen' must be split in two, work and men, for the papers to be gathered between the halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant who drives workers hard is a harsh taskmaster, one who crushes them.

clue.text: Berth that is set back on the outside

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the outside of the abbreviation
set back means the word for set is read backwards

parts.note: to put is to set down
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A ship's berth is said to be set back from the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-up is a mooring place where a boat is secured, just as a berth is.

clue.text: Big star can shed work

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, so the can is removed from the star

parts.note: Canopus is the second-brightest star in the night sky
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big celebrity can get rid of some work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big star' looks like a celebrity but is Canopus, a bright southern star.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary composition, a creative work.

clue.text: Fish expert hooks newt's head maybe once

parts.note: a perch is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the expert catches the newt's letter as with a hook, holding it inside

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fish expert hooks a newt by the head, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old-fashioned word for perhaps, so it meant maybe in former times.

clue.text: Spanish article cut from choice segment

indicators.note: the article is removed from the longer word

parts.note: a selection is a choice
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish piece of writing is trimmed from a chosen segment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' is the grammatical word for the, not a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a part or portion of a whole, a segment.

clue.text: Moved unsteadily, like pack during game?

definitions.meaning: dragging one's feet along in an unsteady walk
a pack of cards is mixed thoroughly before and during play

explanation.surface: Something stumbled about, much like a pack mid-game.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both walking with dragging steps and mixing a deck of cards.

clue.text: Current amount a married traveller raised, period

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word writes it upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A married salesman raised a sum of money for a period.
explanation.definitionFit: Amperage is the strength of an electric current measured in amps.

clue.text: Poet's residence, lavish, hard going

parts.note: a home is a residence

indicators.note: the hard letter departs, removed from the lavish word

parts.note: rich means lavish, opulent
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A poet's lavish home proves hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' is the possessive adjective: belonging to the poet Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeric means relating to Homer, the ancient Greek poet of the Iliad.

clue.text: Actors throw stone about first

indicators.note: the about piece comes first, before the stone

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: Actors are told to toss a stone around first.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple clue: 'Actors' and 'throw' both define the answer, and 'stone about first' builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: The actors in a production are its company, and to throw is to fling or hurl.

clue.text: Bloke's clinched university colours

indicators.note: the bloke grips the university letter inside

parts.note: bloke's read as bloke is, a man, gives the contraction he's

explanation.surface: A man has secured his university colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colours' is not a sports award but simply shades.
explanation.definitionFit: Hues are shades or tints, which are colours.

clue.text: Woman's working on line in fledgling colony

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman
on means working, functioning
RY, railway, is a line

explanation.surface: A woman is working on line in a new colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A heronry is where herons breed in a colony, raising their young fledglings.

clue.text: Young swimmers try out arm supporters

indicators.note: the try word is taken out of the young swimmers

parts.note: goslings are young geese, which swim
a go is a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: Young swimmers try out armbands as supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sling is a bandage hung from the neck to support an injured arm.

clue.text: A Republican disputes quarrels maybe in the past

parts.note: rows are disputes, arguments

explanation.surface: A Republican's disputes are perhaps past quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrels' is not arguments: a quarrel was a crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel was a medieval crossbow bolt, a kind of projectile shot from a bow.

clue.text: What's revealed in cabaret in Raffles Hotel?

indicators.note: the second in shows the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asks what a strip show at the Raffles Hotel lays bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare skin is what a risque cabaret act shows off.

clue.text: Hurried writer, namely bishop, defending Bible (RV)

parts.note: sc., scilicet, means namely

indicators.note: the bishop's letters guard the rearranged word on both sides

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title

indicators.note: RV is the Revised Version of the Bible, so this word is revised, its letters reworked

explanation.surface: A hasty writer, a bishop in fact, defends the Bible's Revised Version.
explanation.walkthrough: '(RV)' looks like a note on the Bible's translation; read as revised version it signals the letters of Bible rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribbler writes quickly and carelessly, a hurried writer or hack.

clue.text: Stream is the same without oxygen

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the same word goes around the oxygen

parts.note: the same as a stream: a burn is a Scottish stream
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A stream stays the same even without its oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like minus, but means outside: BURN goes around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A bourn is a small stream, mostly found in southern English place names.

clue.text: Memorised first of ledger books probed by auditor

indicators.note: the auditor pushes into the other letters, sitting inside them
only the opening letter of ledger is used

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a collection of books
an auditor is a listener, so the hearing organ, an ear

explanation.surface: An accountant memorised the ledger's first entries, and the books were probed by an auditor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant but is literally a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Learnt is the past tense of learn, to commit to memory.

clue.text: A hint of ennui blighted end-of-season bash

indicators.note: spoiled or ruined, so the letters are rearranged
only the final letter of season is used

parts.note: a do is a party, a bash

explanation.surface: A trace of boredom spoiled the end-of-season party.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect suggestion or insinuation, a hint.

clue.text: Dig out study describing energy record

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing a line around, so the study encloses the rest

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room
E is the symbol for energy
an EP, extended play, is a record

explanation.surface: Someone digs out a study about an energy record.
explanation.definitionFit: To deepen a hole is to dig it out further.

clue.text: Outrageous Yankee in shops putting people out

indicators.note: wild and outrageous, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An outrageous American in the shops is putting people out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting people out' is not annoying them but sending them into a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnosis induces a trance-like state, rendering subjects unconscious.
